# Trusted Gradle distribution hosts — SEC-05 control 2 (OPE-216)
#
# `gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties` may point `distributionUrl` at:
#
#   1. the official Gradle publisher, https://services.gradle.org/distributions/
#      gradle-<version>-{bin,all}.zip — always allowed, no entry needed; or
#   2. a host listed below.
#
# Why a host is listed rather than accepted as-is: `distributionUrl` and
# `distributionSha256Sum` are edited independently but must be trusted
# together. Anyone who can edit both in one pull request can otherwise name
# their own host and pin the checksum of their own archive, and the wrapper
# will then download and execute it (threat T10). Requiring `distributionUrl`
# to name a host that is already on this list is what binds the digest to a
# publisher.
#
# The list is empty by default, which is the safe state: this repository builds
# from the official host. A mirror (corporate proxy, internal cache, air-gapped
# artifact server) is a supported configuration — add its host below in a pull
# request that a reviewer approves, changing `distributionUrl` in the same
# commit so the two are reviewed as the single decision they are.
#
# Format: one bare host per line, e.g.
#
#     gradle.internal.example
#     repo.corp.example
#
# Rules (scripts/check-gradle-supply-chain.sh enforces these and fails loudly
# rather than ignoring an entry that could never match):
#
#   * Host only. No scheme, no path, no port, no credentials, no wildcard,
#     no leading dot. `https://repo.example/gradle` and `*.example` are errors.
#   * The host is matched exactly, case-insensitively, against the parsed URL.
#     Listing `example.com` does not allow `cdn.example.com` or
#     `example.com.attacker.test`.
#   * Do not list a host whose TLS certificate you do not control. An entry
#     hands that host's owner the right to choose the bytes your build runs.
#
# No entries.
